name: CA-31
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Gil Cisneros holds a D+8 district and has a roughly nine-to-one fundraising edge over Eric Ching
Prediction markets price Cisneros's win probability near 95 percent
No public general-election polling; the outlook rests on district fundamentals and a Democratic-favoring environment

model.rationale: Cisneros combines incumbency, a large financial advantage, and a district that leans Democratic, and markets price him as a heavy favorite; with no polling to the contrary, the fundamentals point to a comfortable incumbent win.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or a sharp shift in the national environment against Democrats could narrow the margin.

overview:
California's 31st District leans Democratic by eight points, and incumbent Gil Cisneros is seeking reelection with a substantial financial edge. He has raised roughly $853,000 and holds about $213,000 on hand, while Republican Eric Ching has raised under $100,000 with about $10,000 remaining. No significant outside spending has been reported against the incumbent, and prediction markets price his reelection chances at roughly 95 percent.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's fundraising advantage, and market pricing. The political environment currently favors Democrats, adding to the incumbent's structural edge. Ching would need a major influx of resources or a sharp change in the climate to make this competitive. As it stands, the incumbent enters the general election as a clear favorite.
